title: Update on Plans to Review Chinese-Malay-Indian-Others Identity Classification
what_it_is: Update on Plans to Review Chinese-Malay-Indian-Others Identity Classification

sections.label: Race registration by lineage
sections.summary: Individuals can register their race based on lineage, with over 200 races Singaporeans are registered under.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Individuals can register their race based on lineage, and there are currently over 200 different races that Singaporeans are registered under.

sections.label: IPS surveys on race
sections.summary: A 2021 IPS study found 87% of Singapore residents considered race important to identity, and a CNA-IPS survey found over 60% thought CMIO preserved racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: An Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) study in 2021 found that 87%, nearly nine in 10, of Singapore residents considered race important to their identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A 2021 CNA-IPS Survey on Race Relations also found that over 60% of Singapore residents thought that the CMIO policy helped to preserve racial harmony and should be retained.

sections.label: Multiculturalism model review
sections.summary: The multi-racialism model has worked well, but the CMIO framework is reviewed periodically to check its continued relevance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our model of multiculturalism, multi-racialism, with the data and framework we have, has worked quite well for us so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But as Minister Edwin Tong said, we do keep in mind the issue, review periodically, ask ourselves about the CMIO framework, amongst other issues, and see whether it continues to be relevant.

sections.label: Differing views on CMIO
sections.summary: Perspectives differ from Mr Leong on CMIO and the EIP, as shown by his February 2023 Facebook post on HDB living.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Perhaps we have very different perspectives from Mr Leong on CMIO and its implications, for example, on the EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I think that those different perspectives are clear when, for example, you see some of the things that Mr Leong has said in the past, for example, on Housing and Development Board (HDB) living, if you look at Mr Leong's Facebook post of February 2023, and I quote, he says that "Singaporeans are not condemned to living in HDB flat ".

sections.label: Racist statements and undertones
sections.summary: It was said that if party members can think that way, other Singaporeans can reasonably think statements are racist, and Mr Leong acknowledged some may see a racial undertone.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If they can think like that, your own party members, then, other Singaporeans can reasonably think that your statements are racist too.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a simple point." And Mr Leong was good enough to say, "There will be some people who will think that there is racial undertone  , yes".

sections.label: EIP economic cost compensation
sections.summary: The EIP has caused economic disadvantages and costs to minorities, and it was recommended in Parliament that minorities be compensated for that economic cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: What we take issue with is that the EIP has caused economic disadvantages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: There is an economic cost to the minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, we have recommended in this Parliament that we should compensate the minorities for that economic cost they have incurred.
